question: Do the study's hotspots hold under a projected 2030s climate?

source.dataset: DestinE Climate DT, IFS-NEMO, ScenarioMIP SSP3-7.0, generation 1, realization 1, stream clte
source.grid: native HEALPix nside 128 (depth 7, ~51 km), NESTED, on a sphere

params.260048: total precipitation rate (kg m-2 s-1, instantaneous)

source.sampling: 00 and 12 UTC each day, 240 months retrieved and discarded after aggregation

design.why_two_decades: a free-running projection cannot say what a given year was; comparing two decades of the same simulation isolates the climate change, not the weather
design.cell_matching: each WGS84 depth-8 study cell centre looked up in the spherical depth-7 Climate DT grid; support declared as the ~51 km source cell

verdict: unchanged: 96.67% (2020s) and 95.51% (2030s), both far outside the 47.8-68.6% reference range, so the Contradicted conclusion also holds under the projected climate
caveats: Climate DT SSP3-7.0 is served for 2020-2039 only (2018 and 2040 are refused), so the decades are 10 years apart and the forced signal is small (+0.14 degC) relative to internal variability

precipitation is estimated from the instantaneous rate at 00 and 12 UTC, not from accumulated hourly totals; bio12 is 559-585 mm against 635 (ERA5) and 684 (CHELSA), and bio15 is high (67 against 47-51)
the support is a ~51 km source cell, twice the width of the study's cell
the 1.16 pp effect is of the same order as the 0.57 pp gap between our baseline and the published number
free-running projection: these years are plausible years, not observed ones (test 3 used ERA5 for the observed period)
